title: Adjust kitchen cabinet doors
intro: Doors crooked, rubbing or not closing? A screwdriver puts them straight in minutes.

steps.t: Close the doors and look at the gaps: note which door sits higher, sticks out or leans.
Open the door and look at the hinge: usually the screw nearest the door is side, the one behind it depth.
Check each hinge is clipped onto its plate: press the arm until it clicks.
steps.q: Are all the hinges clipped on properly?
steps.fix: Hook the front of the arm on first, then press the back until it clicks. If it wobbles, tighten the plate screws.

steps.t: To move the door sideways, turn the screw nearest the door a quarter turn, the same on every hinge.
If the door leans, turn that screw on the top or bottom hinge only, until the edge runs parallel to the next door.
For depth, turn the rear screw: the door moves in or out until it closes flush with the cabinet.
For height, loosen the plate screws (or turn the cam, if there is one), raise or lower the door and retighten.
Close all the doors and look at the gaps and fronts again.
steps.q: Are the gaps even, about [[2-3 mm]], and the doors flush?
steps.fix: Go back to the screw for that direction and give it another quarter turn: each hinge only moves a few millimetres.

tips: Use a hand screwdriver, not a drill driver: hinge screws are soft and strip easily.
If the door keeps dropping, the plate screws have lost grip in the chipboard: fit slightly thicker screws.
Before adjusting, tighten the screws holding the hinge to the door: often that's the whole problem.

title: Anchor a tall unit to the wall
intro: Tall wardrobe or bookcase? Anchor it so it can't tip over, even if a child climbs it.

steps.t: Put the unit in its final spot against the wall and check it's level and doesn't rock.
Screw the strap's furniture bracket to the top or a side panel, never to the thin back panel.
Run the detector slowly over the wall where you'll drill, both across and up and down.
steps.q: Does the detector stay silent at your drilling spot?
steps.fix: Move the spot at least [[10 cm]] sideways and scan again: the strap can run at a slight angle.
steps.w: Never drill directly above or below sockets and switches: cables usually run straight from them.

steps.t: Knock on the wall: hollow means plasterboard, so find a stud; solid means brick or concrete.
Hold the wall bracket at the same height with the strap taut and mark the holes in pencil.
Drill: no hammer action on brick, hammer on concrete, bit the same size as the plug, e.g. [[6 mm]].
steps.w: Wear safety glasses and hold the drill with both hands, cable away from the bit.

steps.t: Clear the dust from the hole and tap the plug in flush. On plasterboard use a cavity anchor or the stud.
Screw the wall bracket on firmly, stopping before the plug starts to spin.
Hook up the strap, tension it and gently pull the top of the unit towards you.
steps.q: Does the unit stay put when you pull it?
steps.fix: If the plug spins or pulls out, use a longer plug or a cavity anchor; on plasterboard screw into the stud.

tips: Mark the drilling depth on the bit with tape: plug length plus [[5 mm]].
On plasterboard with no stud, use metal cavity anchors: plastic plugs pull out.
Unit wider than [[80 cm]]? Use two straps, one near each side.

title: Assemble a flat-pack chest of drawers
intro: Chest of drawers in a box? Build it square, with drawers that run smoothly.

steps.t: Open the box on the floor, flatten the cardboard and use it as a work mat so the panels don't get scratched.
Count the panels and fittings against the parts list in the manual, code by code.
steps.q: Are all the parts on the list there?
steps.fix: Don't start: note the missing part code and contact the shop, they usually send it free.

steps.t: Sort screws, cam locks, dowels and nails by code into separate bowls.
Push the wooden dowels and cam bolts into the side panel holes, as shown in the drawings.
Join sides, top and base; turn the cam locks clockwise until they grip, about half a turn.
Measure both diagonals of the frame: they should match within [[2 mm]].
steps.q: Are the two diagonals the same?
steps.fix: Gently push the corner of the longer diagonal until they match, then fix the back panel straight away.

steps.t: Slide in the back panel and nail it every [[15 cm]], keeping the frame square.
Screw the drawer runners inside the sides into the pre-drilled holes, same height left and right.
Build each drawer: sides, front, base slid into the grooves, then the back.
Screw the runners to the drawers and slide each drawer onto its runners until it clicks.
Close all the drawers and look at the gaps between the fronts.
steps.q: Are the gaps even and do the drawers run smoothly?
steps.fix: Loosen the runner screws, shift the runner in its slotted holes and retighten. Check the frame is still square.

tips: Stop turning a cam lock as soon as it grips: force it and the chipboard crumbles and won't hold.
Leave screws slightly loose until the whole frame is together, then tighten everything.
Over [[80 cm]] tall? Fix it to the wall against tipping, especially with children at home.
